what: Two v1 behaviors with no v2 counterpart, from v1 crates/blaze-cargo/src/cargo/toolchain.rs, which goes with v1 cargo/ (the v2 copy is now crates/blaze-cargo/src/toolchain{.rs,/}; I left these two out of it). (1) too_new: a package whose rust-version is newer than the Rust blaze ships is refused before building: "`{name}` needs Rust {needs} (its `rust-version`), and this blaze ({release::get().version}) is Rust {ours_release()}: update blaze to one with Rust {needs} or newer, and pin it in the workspace Cargo.toml under `[workspace.metadata.blaze] version`" (cargo: "package `x` cannot be built because it requires rustc N", unless --ignore-rust-version). A nightly counts as its release. Its test: newer_than_ours(1,56,0) is false, ours is false, ours+patch and ours+minor are true. (2) say_toolchain_file: under -v, the nearest rust-toolchain or rust-toolchain.toml above the cwd is said to be ignored: "blaze: {file} is ignored: blaze builds with its own Rust, {ours_release} ({name})"; test the_nearest_toolchain_file_is_found. blaze_cargo::toolchain::{ours_release, name} are there for both. Also FYI: v2 callers now use crate::toolchain and crate::directives (was crate::cargo::{toolchain,directives}); toolchain downloads go through blaze_registry::http::HyperHttp.
